theater: 塞薩利、阿提卡與科林斯

battle.name: 西歌德王國入侵希臘
battle.theater: 塞薩利、阿提卡與科林斯
battle.brief: 395 年狄奧多西一世病逝，帝國東西分立，阿拉里克率西哥德人越過多瑙河入色雷斯，翌年經塞薩利與溫泉關掠劫雅典，再被 Stilicho 以海運援軍逼回北方。卡面秦連弩為中國的連發弩機，並未在此役出現；希臘守城所倚者為石弩與扭力投石機，同樣以壓倒射速把攻城者封在牆外。

kit.name: 秦連弩
kit.history: 弩機把拉力存起來，一踩一發。守城的一方靠它把攻城的人壓在牆外。

countries: 這場戰爭是西歌德聯盟在羅馬帝國東西分裂之際向希臘地區發動的一次大規模掠奪性入侵，時間橫跨 395 至 397 年，真正碰撞的是日耳曼系的西歌德聯盟與羅馬帝國的兩個半邊。西歌德一方並非單一部族，而是以阿拉里克一世為首、聚合了哥特、格皮德與部分阿蘭人的聯盟：首領之下分為若干氏族，每族各有自己的首領與隨從團體，作戰時臨時編為步卒與騎兵混編的隊伍，由族長與百夫長率領；全軍的重大決策依賴部眾集會的認可，這在 4 世紀的哥特社會中仍帶有氏族聯邦的色彩。羅馬一方其實是兩個各自為政的朝廷：西部的皇帝奧勒良駐於米蘭，實際攝政者是野戰軍統帥斯提里科，他掌握兵權與外交；東部的皇帝阿卡狄奧斯駐於君士坦丁堡，樞密院首魯菲努斯以近衛總監身份主持民政，東方野戰軍則交給出身日耳曼的蓋納斯。值得注意的是，交戰的並非「羅馬對蠻族」這樣單純：392 至 395 年間西部的叛將歐根尼烏斯、阿里格魯斯先後起兵，阿拉里克的哥特人曾為狄奧多西一世效力參戰，到 395 年才轉為叛亂；部分史家如湯姆士·伯恩斯甚至主張，這支部隊是由東方樞密院魯菲努斯徵用、派往塞薩利用以牽制斯提里科的棋子。希臘方面的城市與地方守軍屬於被掠奪又被救援的第三方：雅典、科林斯、拉里薩有城牆、駐軍與民兵，足以守住自己的城區，卻無力追擊深入鄉間的掠奪隊伍。羅馬的指揮體系在東方還包括各軍團將官與專職的弩砲隊，在西方則包括能由海路迅速調動的野戰軍與聯邦兵。整場衝突的成敗，最後取決於三方之間的微妙角力：哥特人要的是能合法取得糧食與土地的羅馬承認，斯提里科要的是希臘戰線不致崩潰又不同東方決裂，而君士坦丁堡既想打壓攝政者，也不敢讓哥特人真的在希臘站住腳。
countriesEn: This war was a large predatory incursion launched against the Greek lands by the Visigothic confederation at the moment the Roman Empire split in two, and it ran from 395 to 397. The two great systems that collided were the Germanic Visigothic confederation and the two halves of the Roman state. The Visigothic side was not a single tribe but a coalition gathered around Alaric I, combining Goths, Gepids and a portion of the Alans: beneath the king stood a number of clans, each with its own chieftain and following, mustered for war into mixed bands of infantry and cavalry led by clan captains and centurions, while the weightiest decisions of the whole host depended on the acclamation of the assembled people, a feature that still carried the colouring of a clan federation in fourth-century Gothic society. The Roman side was in fact two separate governments: in the West the emperor Honorius sat at Milan while the real power was the magister militum Stilicho, who held the field army and the conduct of foreign affairs; in the East the emperor Arcadius sat at Constantinople and the praetorian prefect Rufinus presided over civil administration, while the eastern field army was held by Gainas, a man of Germanic origin. Significantly, the opposing parties were not simply Rome against the barbarians: between 392 and 395 the western usurpers Eugenius and Arigerrus rose in turn, and Alaric's Goths had fought for Theodosius I before turning in 395; some historians, such as Thomas Burns, go further and argue that this army was recruited by the eastern minister Rufinus and sent into Thessaly precisely to counter Stilicho. On the Greek side the cities and their local garrisons belonged to the third party, plundered and then relieved: Athens, Corinth and Larissa possessed walls, garrison troops and militia sufficient to hold their own circuits but powerless to pursue raiding parties deep into the countryside. On the Roman command side one must also count the officers of the legions and the specialist ballistarii in the East, and, in the West, a field army and its federate troops that could be shifted quickly by sea. The outcome of the whole conflict was decided by a triangular tension: the Goths needed Roman recognition so that Roman cities would supply them with grain and land; Stilicho needed a Greek front that would not collapse while avoiding a rupture with the East; and Constantinople wanted both to keep the regent in check and to prevent the Goths from establishing themselves in Greece for good.
people: 核心人物是西歌德王阿拉里克一世（約 370 至 411 年）。他出身巴爾幹的哥特社群，幼年隨父輩經歷 378 年亞得里亞堡之敗，隨後在 382 年狄奧多西與哥特人訂立的第一份盟約之下得以進入羅馬軍隊服役，並在哥特出身的將領蓋納斯手下學到羅馬式的用兵；392 年他以羅馬軍職身份作戰，394 年 9 月弗里吉杜斯之役隨狄奧多西出戰，擊敗歐根尼烏斯與阿爾博加斯特，據當時記述其部眾損失約一萬人，而他自己幾乎未受朝廷表彰，只得到羅馬將官級別的認可。狄奧多西一世於 395 年 1 月 17 日病逝於塞薩洛尼基，留下阿卡狄奧斯與奧勒良兩個幼子，羅馬的野戰軍在交接中崩解，這給了阿拉里克脫離控制的空隙。西羅馬攝政斯提里科出身汪達爾與羅馬混血，娶狄奧多西的姪女塞雷娜，395 至 396 年冬天在東巴爾幹擊潰越境者，翌年率西方野戰軍由義大利走海路趕到希臘，以一次出其不意的打擊逼退哥特人，並在 397 年為阿拉里克爭取到伊利利庫姆軍區統帥的頭銜。東方則是樞密院首魯菲努斯與野戰軍統帥蓋納斯的角力：蓋納斯刺殺魯菲努斯後升任色雷斯的軍區統帥，其權勢後來由歐屈羅皮乌斯接替，並在 398 年以擊敗小股匈人的戰果鞏固地位。希臘方面最著名的人物是修辭學家忒彌斯提烏斯，這位在阿卡狄奧斯朝廷任職的哲學家寫下《致狄奧多西書》，以羅馬世界公民與朝廷秩序的語言勸說正在逼近的阿拉里克不要毀滅雅典；晚期史家記載他在交涉時被哥特人殺死。另有一位是傳說中的斯巴達守護者奧努爾福斯：十二世紀的拜占庭編年史稱他顯靈於科林斯地峽，召來風暴摧毀哥特人的船隊，使希臘免於被佔領；史家普遍視之為後世構造的神話，但它直接塑造了後世「希臘未被蠻族征服」的形象。阿拉里克的岳父阿陶爾夫在 395 至 397 年間是其最重要的盟友，日後更成為西歌德王；阿拉里克本人在 411 年病逝於義大利南部的科森扎，葬於布森托河床之下。
peopleEn: The central figure is Alaric I, king of the Visigoths (c. 370 to 411). He grew up in the Gothic communities of the Balkans, spent his boyhood among men who had survived the disaster of Adrianople in 378, and after the treaty of 382, the first of its kind concluded on Roman soil, was able to take service in the Roman army, learning Roman practice of war under the Gothic commander Gainas. From 392 he campaigned with a Roman commission, and in September 394 he fought under Theodosius at the Frigidus, helping to defeat Eugenius and Arbogast; the contemporary record puts the losses of his men in that battle at around ten thousand, while he himself received almost no recognition at court beyond a Roman officer's rank. Theodosius I died of illness at Thessalonica on 17 January 395, leaving the child emperors Arcadius and Honorius, and the Roman field armies fell apart during the handover, which gave Alaric the opening to slip out of Roman control. Stilicho, the regent in the West, was of mixed Vandalo-Roman blood and had married Serena, Theodosius's niece; in the winter of 395 to 396 he defeated an invading band in the eastern Balkans, and in the following year he led the western field army to Greece by sea, striking the Goths unexpectedly and driving them back, and in 397 he secured for Alaric the title of commander of the Illyricum district. In the East the struggle ran between the minister Rufinus and the field commander Gainas: Gainas murdered Rufinus and was raised to command Thrace, and his position was later taken over by Eutropius, who consolidated himself in 398 on the strength of a victory over a small band of Huns in Asia Minor. The best known Greek figure is the rhetorician Themistius, a philosopher in the service of Arcadius's court, who wrote the Epistola ad Theodosium and used the language of Roman citizenship and of the established order of things to urge the approaching Alaric not to destroy Athens; the later historians record that he was killed by the Goths while treating with them. Another figure is the legendary Spartan guardian Onoulphus: twelfth-century Byzantine chronicles say that he manifested himself at the Isthmus of Corinth, summoned a storm that destroyed the Gothic fleet, and so spared Greece from occupation. Modern historians generally treat this as a later fabrication, yet it shaped directly the later image of a Greece that was never conquered by the barbarians. Alaric's father-in-law Ataulf was his most important ally between 395 and 397 and later became king of the Visigoths; Alaric himself died of disease in 411 at Consentia in southern Italy and was buried, according to legend, beneath the bed of the Busento.
kits: 卡面這件秦連弩是中國弩機技術的早期形態：弩機把弦的拉力儲存起來，射手踩動踏板或以腰力拉弦，上弦之後不必再用力，扣下扳機即發一箭。更關鍵的是「連發」：弩身下方設有橫置的彈倉，一次裝填十至三十支小型矢，發射機構每扣一次便推送一支上弦，於是射手可以把注意力全部放在瞄準與射速上。實物上的源流可從戰國至秦漢之交的楚式與秦式銅弩看到，弩機、扳機與彈倉已具備完整形態，漢代南越王墓出土的三十發彈倉弩機是保存最完整的一批；同一設計哲學在蜀漢定型為後人所熟知的諸葛連弩，明清兵書仍沿用「連弩」之名記錄其形制。這件兵器在 395 年的希臘並不存在，必須說清楚：卡面所示之物與本役沒有直接關係。但它的戰術定位在同期地中海有功能等價物，那就是弩砲。希臘與希臘化世界自亞歷山大時代便以胃弩（用絞盤拉伸、射程可達數百米）與手弩砲作為守城主力，羅馬軍中則有把弩臂分解、靠絞盤發射石彈與鉛彈的投射機，以及供守軍連續發射的輕型手弩砲；這些武器同樣遵循「讓城頭火力不被人手速限制」的思路，只是靠的是單發精度、射程與拋物線，而不是連發機構。哥特人一方的裝備完全另一路：雙刃斧、長劍、圓盾與柳條盾、皮甲與早期環甲、長矛，以及從色雷斯山區得來的弓；由於他們在弗里吉杜斯之役前曾為羅馬作戰，軍中相當一部分鎧甲與軍械來自羅馬的徵發與戰利品。攻城器械是希臘方的弱點：哥特人沒有成熟的攻城技術與工匠，只能倚賴突襲、焚燒與快速轉進；羅馬與希臘城市則備有撞槌、可移動的攻城塔、雲梯與掘地道的傳統，東羅馬守軍還有專職的弩砲隊編制。馬匹方面，哥特人靠騎兵做偵察與威嚇，在塞薩利平原有效，在伯羅奔尼撒山區無用；羅馬的關鍵則是海運，斯提里科的部隊由義大利經亞得里亞海與愛奧尼亞海轉運，畜力車與載運船隊把糧秣、攻城器與弓弩手一起送到岸邊，這條補給線在後來的義大利戰場上同樣決定了戰局。
kitsEn: The Qin repeating crossbow on the card is an early form of the Chinese crossbow mechanism: the lock stores the tension of the string, the shooter steps on a treadle or hauls the string with the waist, and once the bow is cocked no further effort is needed, a pull of the trigger loosing one bolt. The crucial point is the repetition: beneath the stock sits a transverse magazine that holds ten to thirty small bolts at a time, and the feed mechanism pushes one bolt forward and re-cocks the bow with every pull, so the archer can devote all his attention to aim and rate of fire. The archaeological lineage of this design is visible in the Chu-style and Qin-style bronze crossbows of the Warring States and early Han, where the lock, the trigger and the magazine are already complete; the thirty-bolt magazine crossbow recovered from the tomb of the king of Nanyue in the Han period is the best preserved series. The same design principle was fixed in the Shu-Han period as the repeating crossbow known to later generations as the Zhuge crossbow, and Ming and Qing military manuals still record the type under the name of repeating crossbow. This weapon did not exist in Greece in 395, and it must be said plainly: the item on the card has no direct connection to this campaign. Its tactical function, however, had an equivalent in the contemporary Mediterranean, and that equivalent was the arrow-shooting machine. The Greek and Hellenistic world had used the belly-gastropletes, cocked by a windlass and with a reach of several hundred metres, and the cheiroballistra as the backbone of city defence since the age of Alexander, while the Roman army had the ballista, with a dismountable bow powered by a windlass that threw stone and lead shot, together with light hand-mounted crossbows for repeated fire by defenders. These machines follow the same logic of keeping the fire of the walls from being limited by how fast a man can pull; they simply rely on accuracy, range and a flat trajectory rather than on a repeating mechanism. The equipment of the Goths belonged to a completely different tradition: double-bladed axes, long swords, round and wicker shields, leather armour and early mail, spears, and bows drawn from the Thracian mountains. Because they had served Rome before the battle of the Frigidus, a good part of the armour and equipment in their ranks came from Roman requisitions and from plunder. Siege engineering was the weak point of the Greek side: the Goths had no mature siege technique and no craftsmen, and could rely only on sudden attack, burning and rapid movement; the Romans and the Greek cities kept the older traditions of the ram, the movable siege tower, scaling ladders and mining, and the eastern Roman garrisons even had specialist units of ballistarii. As for horses, the Goths relied on cavalry for scouting and intimidation, effective on the open plains of Thessaly and useless in the mountains of the Peloponnese; the decisive Roman factor was the sea. Stilicho's troops were carried from Italy through the Adriatic and the Ionian Sea, and wagons and transport hulls brought grain, siege engines and archers together to the landing places; that line of supply would decide the fighting in Italy as much as it did here.
tactics: 哥特人的戰術核心是不攻城、只掠奪。395 年末他們越過多瑙河之後並未選擇攻擊設防良好的要衝，而是讓大隊沿色雷斯的鄉間道路展開，一路燒掠村鎮與莊園，把隊伍分成能快速移動的小股，專挑守軍薄弱或已經空城的目標；羅馬的編年史家馬爾切利努斯記載哥特人劫掠了塞薩利、埃皮魯斯與亞該亞，又北上科林斯與雅典，這正是一種以速度換取收益的戰法。其弱點也來自同一點：沒有基地、沒有穩定糧源、沒有海軍，一旦雨季與寒冬逼迫，隊伍就必須向北方移動，因此在伯羅奔尼撒停留約一年之後，飢餓與疲憊自行把他們推向伊庇魯斯。圍城方面，哥特人在拉里薩一役顯出技術不足：他們能封鎖城外、切割交通，卻沒有能力強攻有石牆與弩砲的城塞，馬爾切利努斯記錄該城未被攻下。羅馬一方在希臘的守城戰術圍繞弩砲展開：城牆的垛口間配置手弩砲與投石機，壓制進攻者的盾陣與雲梯，羅馬軍械帶有大量配重標槍供守軍反擊接近的攻城者；雅典城牆、海路與城內的蓄水池構成一道立體防線，城外的希臘鄉間則靠游擊與傳令求援。斯提里科的解法是典型的以海軍換陸軍：他不等陸上援軍繞行，而是把西方野戰軍由義大利海運至希臘，在哥特人北上途中從側後出擊，然後以歸還掠奪物資、承認其軍職、給予金糧配給的組合，迫其退向多瑙河以南。這種打一下、談一下的節奏，正是 4 世紀末西羅馬對蠻族政策的主軸。補給線上，羅馬依靠海運與沿海城市的穀物、鹽、葡萄酒供應軍隊，冬季退入固定的冬營，避免在希臘山地與野地中因散兵而崩潰；哥特人則必須在戰鬥與追逃之間即時取得糧食，兩者在補給結構上的落差，才是這場戰役最終走向的真正原因。
tacticsEn: The core of the Gothic method was to avoid sieges and simply to plunder. After crossing the Danube in late 395 they chose not to attack well-defended strategic points; instead they spread the host along the country roads of Thrace, burning villages and farmsteads, and split the army into small bodies that could move quickly, picking out targets whose garrisons were weak or whose cities had already been emptied. The Roman chronicler Marcellinus Comes records that the Goths ravaged Thessaly, Epirus and Achaia and then moved north to Corinth and Athens, which is exactly a way of war that trades speed for profit. The weakness came from the same source: no base, no steady supply, no navy, and once the rains and the winter closed in the host had to move north again, so that after roughly a year in the Peloponnese hunger and exhaustion pushed the column towards Epirus by themselves. In siege operations the Goths showed a lack of technique: they could isolate a city and cut its communications, but they had no means of storming a place defended by stone walls and arrow-shooting machines, and Marcellinus records that Larissa was not taken. The Roman side in Greece organised its defence around the missile engines: hand crossbows and stone-throwers were emplaced between the merlons of the walls to crush the testudo of the attackers and the scaling ladders, and the Roman kit carried a large supply of weighted pila for the defenders to use against men who came close to the walls. The walls of Athens, the sea route and the cisterns inside the city together formed a defence in depth, while the Greek countryside beyond the walls relied on skirmishing and on riders carrying the appeal for help. Stilicho's answer was the classic substitution of sea power for land power: rather than wait for reinforcements to make the long circuit, he carried the western field army by sea from Italy to Greece, struck the Goths from the flank while they were moving north, and then combined the return of the plunder, the recognition of Alaric's rank and the grant of money and grain to force the withdrawal towards the Danube. That rhythm of one battle followed by one negotiation was the axis of western Roman policy towards the barbarians at the end of the fourth century. On the supply line, Rome drew grain, salt and wine from the coastal cities and moved them by sea, and went into fixed winter camps rather than dissolving in the Greek mountains and open country; the Goths had to find food on the spot between fighting and marching. The difference in the structure of their supply, rather than any manoeuvre on the field, is the real reason for the way this campaign ended.
data: 有可靠根據的數字並不多，以下只列可核對者。狄奧多西一世於 395 年 1 月 17 日在塞薩洛尼基病逝，帝國此後正式分為東西兩個朝廷，這是阿拉里克在巴爾幹與馬其頓活動的時間框架起點。394 年 9 月 6 日的弗里吉杜斯之役是阿拉里克最後一次為羅馬作戰的大會戰，現代史家依據當時記錄推估其部眾在那一役損失約一萬人，這個數字常被用來說明他後來要求羅馬回報的理由。395 年末至 396 年初，斯提里科在東巴爾幹擊潰另一支越境者。396 年，阿拉里克通過溫泉關進入阿提卡並劫掠雅典，考古層位在雅典多處見到與此役相符的破壞痕跡，年代與史料可以互相對照。掠奪自 396 年起持續約一年，範圍南抵伯羅奔尼撒，北至伊庇魯斯；沿途被劫掠的城市數目，馬爾切利努斯只列了塞薩利、埃皮魯斯、亞該亞、科林斯與雅典等地，沒有給出總數。397 年，阿拉里克獲得伊利利庫姆軍區統帥的頭銜，並取得按人頭供應金糧的權利；399 年東方朝廷把他的管區劃給西方，這一行政動作同時取消了他的軍職與配給，構成他再度叛亂的直接原因。401 至 403 年他進攻義大利，402 年復活節在波倫提亞、同年稍後在維羅納兩度敗於斯提里科。408 年他再圍羅馬，兵力約三萬人，索取的贖金包括約五千磅金、三萬磅銀、四千件絲衣、三千張猩紅染皮與三千磅胡椒，另徵用約四萬名哥特裔奴隸充當軍役。410 年 8 月 24 日起，羅馬城被洗劫三日。411 年阿拉里克病逝於科森扎。就地理而言，戰線自多瑙河下游縱貫巴爾干半島至伯羅奔尼撒南端；溫泉關最窄處的通道被收束到只容車馬通過，數萬人的縱隊在此必須拉成單列，這是行軍上的嚴重限制。至於哥特方面的兵員總數，當時的記錄沒有留下可核對的數字，一般只作數萬人量級的估計。
dataEn: The number of figures that can be checked is small, and only those are listed here. Theodosius I died of illness at Thessalonica on 17 January 395, and the empire was formally divided into an eastern and a western court thereafter; this sets the frame for Alaric's operations in the Balkans and Macedonia. The battle of the Frigidus on 6 September 394 was the last great pitched battle in which Alaric fought for Rome, and modern historians, working from the contemporary record, put the losses of his men in that action at around ten thousand, a figure often used to explain the claim for recompense that he pressed afterwards. In the winter of 395 to 396 Stilicho defeated another band of invaders in the eastern Balkans. In 396 Alaric came through Thermopylae into Attica and sacked Athens, and the archaeological levels in Athens show widespread destruction that can be matched with the written sources in date and in kind. The plunder lasted about a year from 396, reaching south into the Peloponnese and north as far as Epirus; as for the number of cities touched, Marcellinus only names Thessaly, Epirus, Achaea, Corinth and Athens and gives no total. In 397 Alaric received the title of commander of the Illyricum district together with the right to money and grain for the head of each of his men; in 399 the eastern court transferred his district to the West, an administrative act that at one stroke stripped him of his rank and his provisioning and was the direct cause of his renewed revolt. Between 401 and 403 he invaded Italy, and in 402 he was defeated by Stilicho at Pollentia on Easter Sunday and again shortly afterwards at Verona. In 408 he blockaded Rome a second time with a force of about thirty thousand men, and the ransom he demanded included some five thousand pounds of gold, thirty thousand pounds of silver, four thousand silk tunics, three thousand hides dyed scarlet and three thousand pounds of pepper, and he additionally enrolled about forty thousand Gothic slaves into military service. From 24 August 410 the city of Rome was sacked over three days. Alaric died of disease at Consentia in 411. Geographically, the line of operations ran from the lower Danube across the Balkan peninsula to the southern tip of the Peloponnese; the narrowest point of the pass at Thermopylae was constricted to the width of the road, so that a column of tens of thousands had to be strung out in single file, a serious constraint on movement. As for the total size of the Gothic host, the sources of the day left no figure that can be checked, and only an order of magnitude of tens of thousands can be assumed.
cause: 直接原因是一次王朝交接的失控。狄奧多西一世以兩手聯盟維持帝國：他把西部帝位交給奧勒良，讓掌握野戰軍帥印的斯提里科擔任攝政，又把東部交給阿卡狄奧斯並留下樞密院首魯菲努斯加以制衡。395 年 1 月他的猝死讓這個平衡崩掉：兩位少年皇帝無法指揮野戰軍，東西朝廷各自換將，而巴爾干邊境恰好駐著一支已經羅馬化的哥特大軍。深層原因則是 382 年那份盟約的交換條件：哥特人以服役換取和平、可耕種的土地與自治的行政地位，帝國以邊境土地和餉糧換取安全。這份契約一旦停止兌現，哥特人就只剩兩條路，繼續當羅馬的傭兵，或者自立門戶。阿拉里克走的是第二條路：他要求羅馬承認他為眾部眾的首領，並給出相稱的軍職與土地，朝廷只肯給一個羅馬式的將軍銜，作為王的頭銜則一直懸置；這份名分上的落差，成為他與帝國之間最持久、也最能鼓舞部眾的爭議。他於是先把矛頭指向東方首都，重演羅馬內部的叛亂這一模式，期望以軍事逼迫換取承認。至於 395 年這次進攻的幕後推手，史家分成兩派：宮廷詩人克勞狄安把它寫成斯提里科的陰謀，認為攝政者是藉哥特人之手打擊東方同僚；伯恩斯則主張是東方的魯菲努斯徵用阿拉里克去塞薩利，以便在西方反制斯提里科；海瑟與柯林斯等學者又認為核心因素很簡單，阿拉里克需要羅馬的權威來讓羅馬的城市供應他的部眾，而羅馬的機構此時已無法及時回應。無論哪一派更接近真相，結構性的原因都是同一個：帝國把邊防外包給蠻族，卻沒有能力長期兌現契約。
causeEn: The immediate cause was the loss of control during a dynastic handover. Theodosius I held the empire together with a two-handed arrangement: he gave the western throne to Honorius and left Stilicho, who held the marshal's seal of the field army, as regent, and he gave the east to Arcadius with Rufinus, the head of the praetorian office, installed to balance the other side. His sudden death in January 395 broke that balance: two boy emperors could not command the field armies, both courts changed their commanders, and the Balkan frontier happened to hold a Gothic army that had already been Romanised. The deeper cause lies in the exchange terms of the treaty of 382: the Goths gave military service in return for peace, cultivable land and a degree of administrative autonomy, and the empire gave frontier territory and rations in return for security. Once that contract stopped being honoured, the Goths had only two ways left, to remain Roman mercenaries or to stand on their own feet. Alaric took the second road. He demanded that Rome recognise him as the ruler of his people and grant a rank and land to match, and the court would grant only a Roman-style commander's title, while the title of king was left hanging; that discrepancy of rank became the most durable grievance between him and the empire, and the one that best rallied his people. He therefore turned his spear first against the eastern capital, repeating that Roman pattern of internal rebellion and hoping that military pressure would buy recognition. As to who really pushed the invasion of 395, the historians divide: the court poet Claudian wrote it up as a scheme of Stilicho, who used the Goths to strike at his rivals in the east; Burns argues instead that the eastern minister Rufinus employed Alaric in Thessaly in order to counter Stilicho in the west; Heather and Collins among others put the essential factor far more simply, that Alaric needed Roman authority so that Roman cities would supply his people, and that the Roman administration could no longer answer in time. Whichever school is nearer the truth, the structural reason is one and the same: the empire had farmed out its frontier defence to barbarian allies without any means of honouring the bargain for long.
impact: 對希臘，這場入侵是一次難以癒合的裂傷。396 年的劫掠在雅典留下大範圍的破壞層，城市的公共建築與城牆系統受損，古典時代的雅典從此在文學與遊記中以被劫掠的舊都形象出現；科林斯的荒廢更早就被拉丁教會的作家用來見證，例如約 400 年諾拉的保利努斯寫給蘇爾皮西奧斯的信中，描述科林斯已是一片廢墟，而造成這一切的正是蠻人湧入希臘。拉丁作家保利俄斯把劫掠解釋為天罰，認為是希臘城邦的異教過去招致的報應；這套說法後來成為西方上帝之城敘事的一部分。希臘本地則出現相反的另一種記憶：晚期拜占庭編年史所載的奧努爾福斯故事，說一位斯巴達的半神在科林斯地峽顯靈，呼來風暴摧毀哥特艦隊，使哥特人無法渡過地峽；史家普遍視之為後世編造的神話，但它在文藝復興之後被廣為接受，成為拜占庭自我形象的重要組成，即希臘雖屢遭劫掠卻從未被蠻族永久佔領。對羅馬的影響更為結構性：這場戰役確立了以聯邦兵安置取代正面戰爭的處理方式，397 年把阿拉里克升為伊利利庫姆軍區的將軍、給他金糧配給的安排，五年後在義大利重演一次；西羅馬的宮廷因此從米蘭遷往拉文納，帝國的首都第一次落到海邊沼澤與港口的護衛之下。希臘的稅收與糧源在戰後更加難以輸送給西部，而西部對希臘的文化吸引力也隨著城市破壞與人口流散而下降。此外，這場戰役把一位具領袖魅力的蠻族將領推上歐洲舞台中央，其後十五年他將成為西羅馬無法擺脫的變數。
impactEn: For Greece the invasion was a wound that never healed. The plunder of 396 left widespread destruction layers in Athens; the public buildings and the system of walls were damaged, and the classical Athens of the fifth century would thereafter appear in literature and in travellers' accounts as a plundered ancient capital. The ruin of Corinth was recorded even earlier by Latin Christian writers as a sign of the times: in a letter to Sulpicius Severus written around 400, Paulinus of Nola described Corinth as a heap of ruins, and placed the cause in the incursion of the barbarians into Greece. The Latin writer Orosius read the sack as a divine punishment, the just consequence of the pagan past of the Greek city-states, and that reading later became part of the western City of God narrative. In Greece itself a contrary memory took shape: the Onoulphus story in the late Byzantine chronicles, in which a Spartan demigod manifests himself at the Isthmus of Corinth and calls up a storm that destroys the Gothic fleet so that the Goths cannot cross the isthmus. Historians generally treat this as a later fabrication, yet after the Renaissance it was widely accepted and became an important part of the Byzantine image of itself, that Greece, though repeatedly plundered, was never permanently occupied by the barbarians. The effect on Rome was more structural: this campaign settled the practice of settling federate troops in place of fighting a war of annihilation, an arrangement made in 397 when Alaric was raised to command the Illyricum district and given money and grain, and repeated five years later in Italy. The western court consequently moved from Milan to Ravenna, and the imperial capital for the first time sat behind marshes and a harbour. Greek revenue and grain became still harder to send to the west after the war, while the western pull of Greek culture declined as the cities were damaged and their inhabitants dispersed. The campaign also placed a barbarian commander of real personal magnetism at the centre of the European stage, and for the next fifteen years he was a factor the western empire could not shake off.
result: 軍事上，哥特人沒有佔領希臘：雅典被劫掠，拉里薩等設防城市未被攻下，掠奪最遠抵達伯羅奔尼撒，但沒有建立任何常駐政權或分區統治，阿拉里克的隊伍在 396 至 397 年間被逐回多瑙河以南。政治上，這是一場以交換收場的失敗：斯提里科沒有殲滅哥特人，東方的魯菲努斯也沒有因此得到決定性的勝利；結果是 397 年簽成的和解，阿拉里克得到伊利利庫姆軍區的將軍銜、按人頭的金糧配給與在巴爾干的定居權，羅馬則換來數年的安寧。但這份協議從一開始就埋下禍根：399 年東方朝廷把他的管區劃給西方，等於取消他的軍職與配給，於是這支已在帝國境內定居、能合法取用城市物資的軍隊，再次轉為敵人。其後的走向完全可以預見：401 至 403 年他進攻義大利，402 年在波倫提亞與維羅納兩度戰敗；404 至 405 年他駐在潘諾尼亞，像一把懸在東西之間的刀；408 年他再度封鎖羅馬，以封路與斷糧迫使城市交出金銀與物資贖城；410 年 8 月 24 日，他第三次兵臨羅馬城下，羅馬城被洗劫三日，此後三百年裡羅馬城第一次陷落。411 年他病逝於科森扎，屍身依傳說葬在布森托河床之下，帝國隨即重新陷入瓜分聯邦軍的混亂。從更長的視角看，這場戰爭的結果是：它把以聯邦兵守邊境的帝國體制推到極限，第一次證明被帝國雇傭的蠻族首領可以成為西羅馬的主人，而 476 年西羅馬皇帝被廢的終局，也正是在這條線上延伸。
resultEn: Militarily the Goths did not occupy Greece. Athens was plundered, fortified cities such as Larissa were not taken, the raidings reached as far as the Peloponnese, and no lasting administration or regional rule was set up; Alaric's columns were driven back north of the Danube between 396 and 397. Politically this was a failure that ended in a swap: Stilicho had not destroyed the Goths, and Rufinus in the East had won no decisive victory either. What came out of it was the settlement of 397, in which Alaric received the command of the Illyricum district, money and grain for the head of each of his men, and the right to settle in the Balkans, while Rome bought several years of peace. But the arrangement was rotten from the start: in 399 the eastern court transferred his district to the West, which stripped him of his rank and his provisioning, and the army that had already settled inside the empire and could legitimately draw supplies from its cities turned once more into an enemy. What followed was entirely predictable. In 401 to 403 he invaded Italy and was beaten twice by Stilicho, at Pollentia and at Verona, in 402; from 404 to 405 he sat in Pannonia like a knife held between east and west; in 408 he blockaded Rome again, cutting the roads and the grain so that the city had to pay in gold, silver and goods to buy off the siege; and on 24 August 410 he stood before Rome for the third time and the city was sacked over three days, the first fall of the city of Rome in three hundred years. He died of disease at Consentia in 411 and was buried, by legend, beneath the bed of the Busento, and the empire fell back into the confusion of the division of federate troops. From a longer perspective the result of this war is this: it drove the imperial system of defence by federate troops to its limit, and it demonstrated for the first time that a barbarian chief in imperial pay could become master of the western empire. The end of the western empire in 476 lies on the same line.
